subject: ela
intro: Pick the right register (formal or informal).

items.prompt:
For a class presentation, which is more appropriate?
A) Hey everyone, check this out
B) Good morning. Today I will share what I learned.
items.answer: B) Good morning. Today I will share what I learned.

solution.answer: B) Good morning. Today I will share what I learned.

items.prompt:
A letter to your principal should use:
A) formal English
B) slang
C) no greeting

Talking casually with close friends can use:
A) informal English
B) only formal English
C) no words

Which is MORE formal?
A) Yeah, it's cool.
B) Yes, it is interesting.

steps: Complete and polite. Key is B.

items.prompt:
Texting a friend about plans, which fits?
A) wanna hang out Sat?
B) I would like to request your company on Saturday.

steps: Informal fits texting a friend. Key is A.

items.prompt:
In a school report, which is better?
A) The kids were gonna win.
B) The children were going to win.
items.answer: B) The children were going to win.

steps: Formal for reports. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) The children were going to win.

items.prompt:
You are speaking at a school assembly in front of everyone. The BEST choice is to:
A) use formal English with complete, polite sentences
B) use slang and sentence fragments
C) mumble short phrases
items.answer: A) use formal English with complete, polite sentences

solution.answer: A) use formal English with complete, polite sentences

items.prompt:
Which shows the correct use of register?
A) Formal greeting in an email to a teacher; casual words with friends
B) Slang in a letter to the mayor
C) Formal speeches only with friends
items.answer: A) Formal greeting in an email to a teacher; casual words with friends

steps: Match register to context. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) Formal greeting in an email to a teacher; casual words with friends
